blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Built only from the monthly MLS® figures (SnapStats) for condos and townhomes in Central Port Coquitlam. No local notes, sold prices, building list or live listing feed yet; see the open items.

Central Port Coquitlam, Port Coquitlam: 131 condos and townhomes listed at the end of September 2026 and 11 sold in the month, a sales ratio of 8%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market. By listings that is number 1 of 10 Port Coquitlam communities for condos and townhomes.

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. The reports count condos and townhomes together in one line, so this table cannot separate the two. Shares are this community’s count divided by the Port Coquitlam total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Central Port Coquitlam home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

152 condos sold in Central Port Coquitlam with a median price of $572,500 (the middle half sold between $473,750 and $635,000), taking a median of 24 days to sell at 97.7% of the last list price; 5% sold above list. They had a median $627 per square foot, a median year built of 2008 and a median strata fee of $439 a month. 24 townhomes sold in Central Port Coquitlam with a median price of $999,950 (the middle half sold between $757,500 and $1,054,900), taking a median of 18 days to sell at 100.0% of the last list price; 8% sold above list. They had a median $611 per square foot, a median year built of 2024 and a median strata fee of $389 a month.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Central Pt Coquitlam
Montrose Square — 2180 Kelly Avenue

Current listings record the sub-area as Central Pt Coquitlam and the form as Apartment/Condo, freehold strata; one listing states pets and rentals are OK. No source states any age restriction for Montrose Square itself — it is general-market stock, and the 55+ label of the neighbouring Kew rental building must not be borrowed for it. Counted new here.
Symphony at Gates Park — 2488 Kelly Avenue

A boutique apartment-condo building in Central Pt Coquitlam, steps from Gates Park, named in current listing feeds under this name ("Symphony At Gates Park") with the sub-area recorded as Central Pt Coquitlam. Listings record built 2008 and pets as cats OK. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED. Published rental restrictions: UNCONFIRMED. Counted new here.
Lumiere — 2436 Kelly Avenue

An apartment-condo building in downtown Port Coquitlam named consistently across multiple current listings ("LUMIERE," sub-area Central Pt Coquitlam, Apartment/Condo). Year built conflicts: most listings record 2019, one records 2017 — year built UNCONFIRMED between those sources. Listings describe it as pet and rental friendly and wheelchair accessible, with pets allowed with restrictions recorded in one source. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED. Counted new here.
The POCO — 2427 Mary Hill Road

A presale condominium project at Mary Hill Road & Kelly Avenue in Central Port Coquitlam, with an estimated completion of 2028 per the presale source; current listings record units as "built in 2028," freehold strata, 1- to 3-bedroom + den homes from 471 to 1,318 sq ft, with a show home at 2258 Kelly Avenue. The presale source's developer attribution conflicts within its own page (titled "by Rapture Developments"; its FAQ says developed by Azure Properties) — developer: UNCONFIRMED. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED. Counted new here.
Streets, schools and getting around Central Pt Coquitlam

items.t: Central Port Coquitlam is the City of Port Coquitlam's downtown and central area, on the south side of the city between the Coquitlam River and Mary Hill, around Shaughnessy Street and Wilson Avenue, taking in Port Coquitlam Station and the Port Coquitlam Community Centre. Exact board sub-area boundary roads are UNVERIFIED.
Where condo stock concentrates: the downtown Shaughnessy Street / Kelly Avenue / Atkins Avenue shelf. Zoning Bylaw No. 3630 concentrates the apartment zones RA1 and RA2 downtown and along main roads.

Transit: the West Coast Express stops at Port Coquitlam Station in this sub-area — five weekday westbound trains at 6:04, 6:34, 7:04, 7:34 and 8:04 a.m. arriving Waterfront at 6:40–8:40 a.m., and five eastbound returns in the afternoon; no service on weekends or statutory holidays. There is no SkyTrain in Port Coquitlam; TransLink buses connect the city to Coquitlam Central Station, and the R3 Lougheed Hwy RapidBus runs along Lougheed Highway.

Schools and catchments: SD43 catchments are address-based. A School Locator run for the sample address Port Coquitlam Community Centre / Terry Fox Library, 2150 Wilson Avenue — inside this sub-area — returned Central Community Elementary, École Pitt River Middle and École Riverside Secondary (SD43 School Locator Tool, Baragar, run 2026-10-23). Any other address in the sub-area is UNVERIFIED until run.

Recreation: the Port Coquitlam Community Centre, with the Terry Fox Library (Fraser Valley Regional Library), is at 2150 Wilson Avenue downtown; Gates Park is at 2300 Reeve Street, and the Traboulay PoCo Trail loops the city through the central area.
Health: the nearest hospital is Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody — there is no hospital building inside Port Coquitlam.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Central Pt Coquitlam

items.t: Port Coquitlam property taxes: for 2026, due July 2, 2026; a 5% penalty applies to current taxes not paid before end of day July 2, 2026, and an additional 5% penalty applies to current taxes outstanding after September 15, 2026. The City's 2026 increase was 1.95% for the average home, and the City states it has the lowest average property taxes and utility fees in Metro Vancouver; utility bills are flat annual water and sewer fees, billed separately and due March 31, 2026.

blocks.text: Good to know about Central Pt Coquitlam

items.t: Two of the sub-area's biggest buildings have build years that disagree with themselves in public sources. Montrose Square's developer source says 2022 while its listings say 2021 and 2022; Lumiere's listings say 2019 and, in one case, 2017. The discrepancies matter for Newly Built Home Exemption and depreciation-report timing — settle the year from the strata plan and disclosure documents, not from a listing.

The city's one 55+ strata carries a second monthly bill. Mayfair Terrace's mandatory service plan (listing-stated $715/mo for the first resident, $400 for a second) sits on top of strata fees, and the same complex's services side is a registered assisted-living residence under a different street address (Aspira Mayfair Retirement Living, 2267 Kelly Avenue) — a buyer reading only the strata fee is missing half the monthly picture.

There is no SkyTrain coming on any funded timeline a buyer can price. TransLink's Transport 2050: 10-Year Priorities commits only to an "exploratory business case" for extending the Millennium Line to Port Coquitlam, still simply "underway" in the Mayors' Council's Feb 19, 2026 work plan — no route, no stations, no construction funding and no dates approved. Price a downtown condo on the five weekday West Coast Express trains that actually run.

The downtown already had its big rebuild. The $132-million Port Coquitlam Community Centre (205,000 sq ft, 2150 Wilson Ave) fully opened Oct 2, 2021 — three arenas, leisure pool, fitness centre, Terry Fox Library and 425 underground parking stalls — within walking distance of every downtown building in.

Flood infrastructure is mid-upgrade right now. The City's Cedar Drainage Pump Station project, in the dike system at the northeast end of the city, is in tendering with construction set for summer 2026 to summer 2027 and completion expected late summer 2027, funded partly by the Government of Canada.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Central Pt Coquitlam

items.t: Central Pt Coquitlam is the City of Port Coquitlam's downtown and central area, on the south side of the city between the Coquitlam River and Mary Hill, around Shaughnessy Street and Wilson Avenue, taking in Port Coquitlam Station and the Port Coquitlam Community Centre at 2150 Wilson Avenue. The board sub-area name in the SnapStats GVR report is "Central Port Coquitlam"; the City's Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 3838) identifies Downtown as a mixed-use neighbourhood within this part of the city. Exact board sub-area boundary roads are UNVERIFIED.
Nearby areas: Mary Hill and Riverwood to the north and east, Glenwood PQ and Citadel PQ on the north side across the tracks and Lougheed Highway, Coquitlam to the west across the Coquitlam River.

Port Coquitlam community figures (sub-area medians are NOT published: UNVERIFIED at sub-area level): detached median $1,262,500, $563/sq ft, 97% sale-to-list, 42 days; attached median $660,000, $613/sq ft, 95% sale-to-list, 27 days.

Zoning Bylaw No. 3630 concentrates apartment zones RA1 and RA2 downtown and along main roads, and also carries townhouse zones RTh1, RTh2 and RTh3 and a rowhouse zone RRh city-wide — a zone existing in the bylaw is not a named complex in this sub-area.

Schools: SD43 Coquitlam, catchments address-based. A completed SD43 School Locator run documented in this sub-area's own research (Baragar, run 2026-10-23) for 2150 Wilson Avenue returned Central Community Elementary, École Pitt River Middle and École Riverside Secondary — Ministry-listed names in that form. Catchments for any other specific address are UNVERIFIED without its own locator run.

Roads: Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) and the Mary Hill Bypass (Highway 7B) cross the city; Shaughnessy Street and Coast Meridian Road are the main north–south routes. Driving commute times: UNVERIFIED — no official source publishes them.

Recreation: Port Coquitlam Community Centre with the Terry Fox Library (Fraser Valley Regional Library) at 2150 Wilson Avenue; Gates Park at 2300 Reeve Street; the Traboulay PoCo Trail loops the city along the riverfront; Colony Farm Regional Park (Metro Vancouver) sits on the Coquitlam River at the city's west edge. Port Coquitlam is the hometown of Terry Fox; the Terry Fox: Inspiring Local Champions exhibit is at the Community Centre.

Hospital: Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody (Fraser Health); Royal Columbian Hospital in New Westminster is the larger regional hospital. No hospital building inside Port Coquitlam was verified.

items.t: Form B diligence (any strata purchase): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.

: there is no SkyTrain station inside Port Coquitlam. An extension is an exploratory business case only in the Mayors' Council Feb 19, 2026 work plan — no funding, no route, no dates exist to price into a purchase.

blocks.text: Good to know about Central Pt Coquitlam

items.t: The city's deepest attached shelf contains no verified townhouse complex.

The city's one 55+ strata carries a second monthly bill, and its services side has a different address. Mayfair Terrace's mandatory service plan (listing-stated $715/mo first resident, $400 second) sits on top of strata fees, and the services side of the same complex is registered as Aspira Mayfair Retirement Living, 2267 Kelly Avenue — a buyer reading only the strata fee is missing half the monthly picture.

The newest 55+ building downtown cannot be bought. Kew Lifestyles at Montrose (2430 Mary Hill Rd, 56 units, completed 2023) sits beside Montrose Square (2180 Kelly Ave, general-market) — the two share a developer area and a street, but only Kew is 55+, and Kew is rental only. Do not borrow its label for its neighbour.
Two well-known Tri-Cities 55+ buildings are not in this city at all.

The zoning bylaw promises townhouse zones the sub-area hasn't produced as named complexes. Bylaw No. 3630 carries RTh1, RTh2, RTh3 and RRh zones city-wide, but downtown's built attached form is the RA1/RA2 apartment shelf — zone names in a bylaw are not stock.

Flood infrastructure is mid-upgrade. The City's Cedar Drainage Pump Station project, in the dike system at the northeast end of the city, is in tendering with construction set for summer 2026 to summer 2027 and completion expected late summer 2027, funded partly by the Government of Canada.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Central Port Coquitlam?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 131 condos and townhomes listed in Central Port Coquitlam. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Central Port Coquitlam a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In September 2026, condos and townhomes in Central Port Coquitlam had a sales ratio of 8%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Central Port Coquitlam from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 77 condos and townhomes sold in Central Port Coquitlam over those 4 months, out of 151 in all of Port Coquitlam.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: What did condos in Central Port Coquitlam sell for?
faq.a: 152 condos sold in Central Port Coquitlam between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $572,500.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in Central Port Coquitlam?
faq.a: The median was 24 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.7% of the last list price (5% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

One strata: Mayfair Terrace (2266 Atkins Ave, LMS4171, built 2000, 46 units, published 55+). Kew Lifestyles at Montrose is also 55+ but it is purpose-built rental — nothing to buy. The Shaughnessy and Montrose Square are general-market and NOT age-restricted.

faq.q: What does buying at Mayfair Terrace commit me to beyond strata fees?
faq.a: A mandatory base service plan on top of strata fees — a current listing states $715/mo for the first resident and $400 for a second, covering daily breakfasts plus 10 meals, weekly housekeeping, 24-hour emergency response, activities and transportation (listing-stated figures). Confirm the current amounts and terms against the strata documents and the service agreement before relying on them.

faq.q: Montrose Square sits beside a 55+ building — is Montrose Square 55+ too?
faq.a: No. Montrose Square (2180 Kelly Ave, 364 strata units by Quantum Properties) is general-market strata; the 55+ building beside it is Kew Lifestyles at Montrose (2430 Mary Hill Rd), which is rental only. Do not borrow Kew's label for Montrose Square.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Central Pt Coquitlam condo long-term?
faq.a: Yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC, including the restriction element in Shaughnessy Square's directory line. A registered 55+ bylaw (Mayfair Terrace) still limits who may live in the unit.

faq.q: How did Central Pt Coquitlam sell in September 2026?
A downtown listing calls a unit a "townhome" inside a condo tower — is it a townhouse complex?

faq.a: No. The West Coast Express stops at Port Coquitlam Station in this sub-area; the Millennium Line is reached by bus at Coquitlam Central. A PoCo SkyTrain extension is an exploratory business case only — no funding, route or dates.

faq.q: Is there a 55+ townhouse I can buy downtown?
faq.a: No verified 55+ townhouse complex exists in PoCo. The city's one verified 55+ ownership complex is Mayfair Terrace (2266 Atkins Ave, LMS4171, built 2000, 46 units) — apartment-form, counted in condos, with a mandatory Aspira service plan ($715/mo first resident / $400 second, listing-stated) on top of strata fees. Kew Lifestyles at Montrose is 55+ rental — nothing to buy.
